room_or_space: Exterior: south elevation of the whole building (drawing titled SOUTH ELEVATION); no interior room is shown

proportions.notable_proportion: No dimensions or scale are written. Visually the elevation is extremely horizontal: the full facade is roughly six to seven times as long as the main block is tall from ground line to main eave, and each hipped roof overhangs its walls by roughly a window-bay at each end. The window bands are much taller than they are wide per light, and the upper storey block is roughly a third of the length of the main block and sits near the centre.

layout.organisation: Stacked horizontal layers: a continuous low base and terrace/garden walls with light copings; above it a two-level main block (a lower band of short windows, a brick spandrel, then a tall band of casement windows directly under a very wide low-pitched hipped roof); a smaller third-storey block set back and centred on the main block with its own hipped roof and a chimney mass; and at the right a lower two-level wing with its own hipped roof, a porch-like ground level, paired doors and a low walled enclosure at the far right.
layout.axes: A single dominant horizontal axis running the full length of the facade, reinforced by the roof fascias, the window-band heads and sills, the copings and the horizontal brick coursing. A secondary near-central vertical emphasis is given by the set-back upper storey and its chimney; the roofs are symmetrical about their own centres but the whole facade is asymmetrical, longer and lower to the right.
layout.entry_sequence: The main block shows no door on this face. The only doors are a pair of doors at ground level of the right-hand wing, set behind a low terrace/garden wall with a light coping; they are reached across the enclosed terrace. Two low walls with copings and urns on piers front the main block at ground level.
layout.circulation: Exterior only; no interior circulation is drawn. The ground level reads as a series of enclosed terraces behind low walls, with the paired doors at the right wing as the only opening through the wall plane shown.

openings.position: Main block, upper (principal) floor: a continuous run of roughly twenty tall narrow casement windows directly under the main eave, from the left end of the block to the start of the right wing
openings.pattern: Each window has a thin frame and one to three thin vertical mullions; windows are separated by narrow brick piers; the band has a continuous head at the eave and a continuous sill line

openings.position: Main block, lower (ground) level: a band of about fourteen shorter, nearly square windows between brick piers, below a brick spandrel and above the base coping
openings.pattern: Regular repeat matching the window rhythm above; each window a simple framed light with one mullion; the band stops at the pier carrying the right-hand urn

openings.position: Upper storey (third level) set-back block: a band of about nine or ten casement windows under its own eave, with a single wider window to the left of the chimney
openings.pattern: Same tall narrow casement module as the main floor, continuous head and sill; brick piers between windows

openings.position: Right wing, upper level: a band of about eight casement windows under the wing's hipped roof
openings.pattern: Same tall narrow casement module as the main block, separated by narrow piers

openings.position: Right wing, ground level: a group of wider windows either side of the paired doors, including one window with a geometric leaded-glass lattice pattern at the left end of the porch bay
openings.pattern: Wider, squarer lights than the upper bands; sills sit on a low brick wall with coping; one window shows a diamond/geometric lattice in its glazing

openings.position: Right wing, ground level, roughly a third of the way in from the right end of the facade, behind the terrace wall
openings.pattern: A pair of door leaves separated by a post, each with a glazed upper panel and a lower panel drawn with vertical boarding

openings.position: Far right, low walled enclosure: a single small window set in the low wall at the right end of the facade
openings.pattern: Single framed light with one mullion, under a short cap

openings.position: Top of chimney mass above the upper storey roof
openings.pattern: A rectangular louvered or slatted vent slot in the left half of the chimney head

details: Deeply cantilevered low hipped roofs with thin fascias, overhanging the walls by roughly a bay at each end; the main roof extends over the start of the right wing
Continuous bands of tall narrow casement windows set directly under the eaves, with repeated thin vertical mullions and narrow brick piers between
Brickwork drawn as long thin courses with only horizontal joints shown, and every wall, pier and sill capped by a light smooth coping band
Low stepped terrace and garden walls with copings, carrying two wide shallow urns on piers at the junctions between wall heights
A geometric leaded-glass lattice in one ground-floor window of the right wing, and a louvered vent slot in the chimney head
